text:
The vote passed. The system didn't move.

You sit with that for one night, and then you stop sitting with it.

Caden finds you the next morning. He doesn't say anything for a moment — he just looks at you with the specific attention of someone who has been measuring you against something and has come to a conclusion. Then:

"So we go around it."

Not a question. Not a proposal. A statement of direction.

Sera has the administrative records — her grandmother's name on a VOIDED classification seal, which is the kind of evidence that is uncomfortable for an institution because it requires the institution to reckon with its own history rather than simply contesting the data. She has been building a case for two years. The case is almost complete.

The original Commission files are still in the Conclave's secure archive. Ines can get them out, if there is something to do with them when they arrive.

You have what you have: a piece of the truth, two people who showed up when it mattered, and a direction.

It is not a plan yet.

It is something better than a plan: it is a commitment to find the plan. Sometimes that's the same thing.
